_note: Written only by the bi-weekly growth review. Embedded in every brief as review_rules. Each rule cites its evidence; the next review keeps, changes or drops it.

rules.rule: First line = one concrete moment + what the person pretended or hid in it ("I smiled in every photo", "he told us he was at work", "I replied okay so he wouldn't see me cry"). Keep it under ~18 words so it can be read on mute in the first 2-3 seconds.
rules.evidence: Last 14 days: JR-0045 (IG 2,251 views, 67 saves, best of the window), JR-0020 earlier (1,909 / 48 saves), JR-0040 (IG 1,659 + YT 1,201), JR-0046 (YT 1,315) all open on a hidden feeling. Mosseri: watch time and the first seconds gate distribution (kompozy.io, 2026-09-25); YouTube Shorts: viewed vs swiped away is the core signal (outlierkit.com, 2026-10-03).

rules.rule: Avoid 'worried about the future' episodes (money next month, will I belong, going back to church someday). If the topic is a worry, set it in a present, concrete scene that already happened today, and label the emotion sad/hurt, not worried. At most 1 per week.
rules.evidence: emotion=worried: JR-0024 247, JR-0037 198, JR-0030 1,287 IG views vs window median 1,370; flagged already on 2026-10-11 (IG median 280, n=4).

rules.rule: The engagement line is a send line that names one specific person ("Send this to the friend who..."). Never 'type a prayer', 'comment amen', 'tag a friend'.
rules.evidence: Sends per reach is Instagram's strongest signal for non-followers (Mosseri, restated 2026-09-25, kompozy.io). JR-0053 old version still said 'Type a prayer...' and was fixed in this review.

rules.rule: Write the closing question so it can be answered in one line on YouTube too; the review replies to YouTube comments from Studio.
rules.evidence: Last 14 days: 32 comments on 26 YouTube Shorts vs 4 on 26 Instagram Reels.
rules.note: 2026-11-05 (R13): the answerable question now goes in first_comment (pinned on YouTube by the comment run, posted by Buffer on Instagram); the caption may still carry one small question.

rules.rule: Never set an episode in another faith's festival, ritual or practice (Diwali, puja, festival lamps, rangoli, Holi, Navratri, Eid, temple visits, karma, astrology). Indian family life stays welcome (Amma, Appa, aunties, trains home, office, hostel); use neutral everyday moments or the Christian calendar (Sunday service, Advent, Christmas, Good Friday, Easter, a church wedding). Seasonal hooks come from the Christian year or from secular life (exams, salary day, monsoon, new year), never from another religion's worship. Enforced: safety.faith_framing holds any hit for review.
rules.evidence: JR-0071..JR-0078 ran five Diwali-framed episodes in a row (JR-0076 had Jesus saying 'You missed the puja' and 'The lamps need you'). YouTube viewer, 2026-10-28: 'Why would Jesus be ok with stuff to do with Diwali. The makers of this video gladly let go off the first commandment' (Exodus 20:3). Selvin, 2026-10-29: fix it, rework the strategy and schedules.

rules.rule: Keep total spoken words (all lines + verse) at 95-120. Over 130 words is a rewrite, not a trim. Split any line that runs past ~4s (about 10 words at 150 wpm) and change the frame inside it.
rules.evidence: skill_review calibration 2026-10-29 (n=47 per platform): IG top quartile median 110 words (~44s, 1,836 views) vs bottom quartile 157 words (~63s, 199 views); r(length, log views) = -0.43 IG, -0.22 YT. YT top quartile 115 words. Generic ig-reel hookscore does NOT predict our views (IG r=0.19, YT r=-0.30), so it stays advisory only.

rules.rule: Every script names in its brief WHO would send it and TO WHOM (e.g. 'a friend going through a breakup'). If nobody would forward it, rewrite the angle. No comment-bait or 'type amen' CTAs.
rules.evidence: Mosseri 2026-10-23: sends matter far more than comments, especially for non-followers. Our IG sends/reach r=0.27 with log views vs likes/reach r=-0.06.

rules.rule: Frame 1 shows the viewer's problem as on-screen text readable without sound, within 1s. The first spoken line states the topic. No logo, title card or slow fade-in.
rules.evidence: YouTube Shorts gate = viewed vs swiped away. IG avg watch time 11.1s median is our strongest view predictor (r=0.40).

rules.rule: The last line gives a reason to follow, tied to the series (e.g. 'Jesus replies to a new struggle every morning'). Never beg. One line, under 3s.
rules.evidence: 0 followers gained across 35 IG reels with ~1.2K median reach: strangers watch but don't convert.
rules.note: 2026-11-05 (R12): the script's last line is now the share line; the follow reason lives in the caption's series line ('New question every morning and night.').

rules.rule: The verse must mean, in its own passage, what the episode uses it for. Read the 3-5 verses around it before pairing. No proof-texting (e.g. Matthew 5:37 is about oaths, not lending boundaries). If no verse fits honestly, change the topic, not the meaning. Scripture is the KJV, quoted verbatim (DEC-JR-016); a correct quotation never excuses a wrong context.
rules.evidence: JR-0077 (IG, 2026-10-30) paired Matthew 5:37 (oaths, Matt 5:33-37) with saying no to a friend borrowing money; top comment: 'worst translation of Matthew 5:37'. The wording was verbatim (BSB at the time; KJV since 2026-11-05); the misuse was the context.

rules.rule: Line 1 is a confession ("Jesus... I said yes again.") or a statement ("Jesus... my brother's EMI is on my card now."), never a question: no '?' and no why/how/what/is/does opener. One script feeds Instagram and YouTube, so it holds for both. The validator fails a question opener from JR-0094 on, and the planner only assigns confession/statement hook strategies.
rules.evidence: YouTube median views by hook type: question 382 (n=41), statement 1,270 (n=11), confession 1,440 (n=24). Instagram is neutral: question 1,526, statement 1,559, confession 1,319. learnings.json already listed hook_type=question under avoid (episode score 0.31 vs 0.52, n=21). Selvin approved 2026-11-05.

rules.rule: The script's last line (speaker 'engagement') is a share line in the channel voice that names who needs it ("Send this to someone who needs it today."), worded freshly each episode (the validator rejects a word-for-word repeat of the last 7). The caption carries a share line too. Never 'type amen', 'comment', 'tag' or other bait. Replaces the closing question; the question moves to the first comment (R13). Builds on R3.
rules.evidence: Sends per reach is Instagram's strongest signal for reaching non-followers (Mosseri 2026-10-23); our sends/reach r=0.27 with log views vs likes/reach r=-0.06. Selvin approved 2026-11-05.

rules.rule: Every new package has first_comment: one easy, warm question tied to the episode, at most 150 characters, no links, hashtags or bait ("Has someone in your family ever said this to you?"). Instagram: Buffer's firstComment is a paid feature (rejected 2026-11-05), so the comment run posts it under each new Reel by hand until publishing-rules buffer.instagram_first_comment is true. YouTube: Buffer has no first-comment field, so the every-2-days comment run posts it from the channel and pins it (comment-replies.md).
rules.evidence: Comments are near zero on Instagram (4 on 26 Reels) but YouTube is where people answer (R4). A seeded, answerable question gives viewers an easy first reply. Selvin approved 2026-11-05.

rules.rule: A 'Jesus replies to your comment' episode uses a real comment logged in content-os/community/, quoted exactly, respectful, never a crisis comment, critique or bait; the handle is hidden on screen unless config comment_reply.show_handle allows it. One a week (Thursday 19:30). Enforced by daily/formats.comment_problems.
rules.evidence: YouTube is where viewers talk (R4: 32 comments vs 4 on IG in 14 days); answering one on screen rewards commenting. Selvin approved 2026-11-05 (DEC-JR-018).

rules.rule: Tamil/Hindi subtitle versions: story lines are natural human translations; the verse caption is the bundled IRV text (CC BY-SA 4.0, Bridge Connectivity Solutions) for the same reference, verbatim, never machine-translated; the attribution line is in caption and description. The spoken/English verse stays KJV. Enforced by daily/formats.subtitle_problems + package_problems.
rules.evidence: Audience is largely Indian (Tamil/Hindi family themes perform best: JR-0060, JR-0071). Selvin approved 2026-11-05 (DEC-JR-018).

experiments.plan: YouTube: second Short at 13:00 IST instead of 20:30 for 14 days; keep IG at 08:00/20:30. Compare 7-day engaged-view medians vs 20:30 baseline (611).
Enable Instagram AI translations/dubbing (opt-in in app) for reels with speech; compare reach and non-follower share for 14 days.
Evening slot 19:30 IST on both platforms vs 20:30 baseline (IG 1,358, YT 611). Read 2026-11-12, decision rule in experiments.json.
experiments.note: 2026-11-05 (Selvin, DEC-JR-017): no slot change now (never change slots on n<10). At the 2026-11-12 read, also weigh moving YouTube's evening post to a morning slot at 05:00 IST against 19:30: 05:00 is 3 h before the 08:00 post and 18:30 US Eastern (YouTube's audience is US-led, ~44%). Evidence to carry into that read: YouTube 08:00 median 1,198 views (n=24) vs the old 20:30 median 725 (n=27); 19:30 has n=2 so far. Instagram slots stay 08:00/19:30. A move applies only to posts not yet in Buffer and needs n>=10 on the YouTube evening arm.
